questions.stem: What is the product of two negative integers?
questions.solution: The product of two negative integers is a positive integer because multiplying two negative numbers results in a positive number due to the rules of sign multiplication. A negative integer is incorrect because the negatives cancel each other out. Zero and fractions are not possible because the product of two integers is always an integer, and two negatives cannot result in zero.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the product of a positive and a negative integer?
questions.solution: The product of a positive and a negative integer is always negative. (−7) × 2 results in a negative number, making it the correct example. (−5) × (−3) and 6 × 4 result in positive numbers, while 8 × (−3) is also a valid example of a negative product, but (−7) × 2 is explicitly the correct choice here.

questions.stem: If (−6) × x = −18, what is the value of x?
questions.solution: To solve (−6) × x = −18, divide both sides by −6, which gives x = 3. This is correct because multiplying −6 by 3 results in −18. Choosing −3 would result in a positive 18, 6 would result in −36, and −6 would result in 36, none of which match the equation.

hi.solution: समीकरण (−6) × x = −18 को हल करने के लिए दोनों ओर −6 से भाग देते हैं, जिससे x = 3 प्राप्त होता है। यह सही है क्योंकि −6 को 3 से गुणा करने पर −18 प्राप्त होता है। −3 चुनने पर धनात्मक 18 प्राप्त होता है, 6 चुनने पर −36 प्राप्त होता है और −6 चुनने पर 36 प्राप्त होता है, जो कोई भी समीकरण के साथ मेल नहीं खाता।

questions.stem: If (−4) × (−7) = 28, which of the following is also true?
questions.solution: The commutative property of multiplication states that changing the order of the numbers does not change the product, so (−7) × (−4) = 28, just like (−4) × (−7) = 28. The other options incorrectly change the sign of the product or the order of the numbers, which would alter the result.
